job.title: Strategic Paraplanner
job.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

You’ll be joining a highly regarded Australian wealth management and stockbroking firm with a long history of helping private clients build and protect their wealth. The firm is known for high calibre advisers, a collaborative culture and real investment in its people. It is growing its adviser numbers and gives talented paraplanners a real path into private wealth. Staff value the strong brand, the sophisticated client base and the chance to learn from some of the most experienced advisers in the industry.


ABOUT THE ROLE
 
Reporting to the Strategic Advice Lead, you'll join a small, experienced strategic advice team based in offices around Australia. The role goes beyond standard paraplanning.
 
You'll produce high quality SOAs, and you'll also work with advisers on client strategy, research technical issues and help shape the advice given to high net worth clients. It's an excellent stepping stone into private wealth: the person who held this role before you is moving into the private wealth team.
 
DUTIES
  • Prepare complex SOAs and ROAs from adviser briefs
  • Build financial projections and models for high net worth clients
  • Advise advisers on strategy and on the advice process
  • Research technical strategy using a wide range of resources
  • Collect accurate information from insurance and superannuation providers
  • Keep all advice documentation compliant from preparation through to delivery
  • Guide private wealth assistants as they implement advice
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • A tertiary qualification in financial planning or a related field
  • The Financial Adviser Education Standard completed or underway
  • 2 to 3+ years of paraplanning experience, with strong SOA writing skills
  • Solid Xplan skills, including SOA generation (Client Focus, Risk Researcher, WealthSolver, XTools+, IPS)
  • Advanced Word and Excel, with good financial modelling and analysis
  • A sound understanding of the advice process, structures, entities, products and compliance
  • Desirable: interest in becoming an adviser in the future
BENEFITS
  • A competitive package of up to $115,000
  • Eligibility for a discretionary bonus
  • A clear career path into private wealth and advice
  • Exposure to complex strategy and high net worth clients
  • Mentoring from a senior strategic advice team

job.title: Executive Director of Members, Volunteers & Early Intervention
job.description:
ROLE DETAILS
  • Generous salary package with PBI salary packaging
  • Flexible location across NSW, with a preference for Sydney
  • Hybrid working with WFH flexibility, plus regular travel across NSW
  • Permanent, full time
  • Some weekend commitments, around six per year
ABOUT THE COMPANY
The St Vincent de Paul Society NSW, otherwise known as Vinnies, is one of Australia's best known charities. Grounded in its lay Catholic heritage, Vinnies works to reduce the impact of poverty and address injustice, offering a hand up to people experiencing disadvantage. Members, volunteers and staff work side by side in communities across NSW, delivering practical assistance, specialist services and advocacy. It is a values driven organisation where people are united by a shared mission and a genuine commitment to the communities they serve.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Reporting to the CEO as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you will lead the Membership, Volunteers and Early Intervention directorate. This is the primary link between Vinnies and its members, from local Conferences through to State Council. You will lead five Regional Directors and a Director, Programs, and oversee major programs including Vinnies Vans, Disaster Recovery, NILS and the early intervention work of Conferences. You will shape the future of membership and build trust across a unique governance model.

DUTIES
  • Lead the directorate to deliver key priorities in the strategic plan and contribute to the next enterprise strategy
  • Build trusted, transparent relationships with the State Council President, State Council and Central Council Presidents
  • Drive member recruitment, renewal and retention so Conferences remain active and sustainable
  • Strengthen the experience and engagement of members and volunteers, supporting participation, connection and long-term sustainability
  • Develop and implement statewide member, youth and volunteer engagement strategies
  • Lead new ways of working, including regional operating model, to strengthen collaboration, consistency and connection across the Society
  • Oversee delivery of member programs including Conference assistance, WE CARE, NILS, Vinnies Vans and Disaster Recovery
  • Ensure quality and measurable community outcomes across member programs and early interventions services.
  • Represent Vinnies with government, ministers, major donors and corporate partners to grow funding and partnerships
  • Develop the capability of Regional Directors and their teams, leading people to be their best
  • Oversee directorate budgets, resources and performance, driving financial sustainability and continuous improvement.
  • Strengthen governance, compliance and risk management across members, volunteers and staff
  • Partner with Executive Directors across Services, Retail and Finance to deliver a "One Society" approach
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Senior executive experience leading large, dispersed teams and complex programs
  • Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into operational improvements and lead change across complex, geographically dispersed locations
  • Experience in a membership based organisation, union, peak body or similar environment
  • Exceptional stakeholder management and political judgement, with the maturity to anticipate issues early and negotiate outcomes
  • Credibility and confidence with government, funders and major donors
  • Strong understanding of governance, compliance and risk
  • Genuine alignment with the mission and respect for the Society's lay Catholic heritage and values
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications
  • Desirable: experience in the not for profit, social services or faith based sectors
BENEFITS
  • Generous salary package
  • PBI salary packaging to increase your take home pay
  • Five weeks of annual leave
  • Executive Leadership Team role reporting directly to the CEO
  • Flexible location across NSW with hybrid working and WFH
  • The chance to make a real difference for around 105,000 people each year

Recruitment Consultant

Job Type
Permanent

Job Location
Sydney NSW 2000

Salary
$75,000-$100,000

In order to be successful in this high-performing environment, you will be a self-starter, team-oriented in how you work, happy to recruit at a very fast pace, value relationships above all else and hold yourself to very high standards of work. Our next team member will not just be looking for a job, they are looking to be part of a team that really cares about what they do.

  • Genuine opportunities for growth and development
  • A great office vibe! - Music, snacks, a 'dress for your day' dress code and an inclusive, friendly environment

job.description:

Lotus People are delighted to be partnering with a rapidly growing and innovative business operating within the life insurance and financial advice sector.

Having experienced significant growth over the past few years, this business provides a unique combination of licensing, technology and operational support to financial advice practices across Australia.

With a collaborative, energetic culture and a strong focus on innovation, they are passionate about empowering their people, embracing new technology and continuously improving the way they operate.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Life Insurance Administration Manager to take ownership of a key operational function within the business.

Leading a small team across Australia and offshore, you will oversee the day-to-day life insurance administration function, ensuring workflows are managed effectively, service standards are met and the team is supported to perform at its best.

This is a genuinely hands-on leadership opportunity, ideal for someone who enjoys mentoring others while remaining actively involved in complex cases, escalations and operational activities.

With the business continuing to grow, you will also play an important role in identifying efficiencies, streamlining processes and driving continuous improvement.

We are looking for a proactive, resilient and engaging leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys making a difference.

You will bring strong administration experience within life insurance or a closely related financial services environment, alongside demonstrated experience leading, coaching or supervising others.

To be successful, you will ideally have:

  • Strong understanding of administration workflows, outstanding requirements and case management processes.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • A proactive mindset with a passion for improving processes and driving efficiencies.

Above all, you will be someone who brings energy, accountability and initiative to the team. You will be comfortable sharing ideas, embracing change and rolling up your sleeves to get things done.
